children: Telstra gains a bull in Citi, which thinks its Ebitda--or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization--could top market expectations because of stronger cost control. Citi also views Australia's largest telco as being well placed to deliver 5% year-over-year growth in mobile services in FY27, "with potential upside from stronger ARPU [average revenue per user] growth." While an inquiry into regional mobile coverage across Australia and a potential medium-term headwind to ARPU from proposed legislative changes are risks to consider, "we see Telstra as defensive in a soft macro environment," Citi says. It upgrades the stock to buy from neutral. It keeps a target price of 5.25 Australian dollars a share. The stock is up 0.2% at A$4.73. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
